Siemens SOMATOM Force: Dual-Source Dual Energy

One dual-source scan of the Gammex 472 on the Siemens SOMATOM Force, 100 kVp on tube A and Sn140 kVp on tube B, read two ways: as the routine mixed image and as virtual monoenergetic images (VMIs).

The Force's UFC scintillator enters through BasisMonteCarlo's Geant4 table, and the VMI chain is the one of the basis-spectral-denoising study: one projection per tube shared by every noise draw, a noise-free reference, SpectralHYPR, and the spectral pair fixed from a calibration draw.

The Force is not inherently spectral: routine protocols run both tubes at the same kVp, and dual energy is a mode. In that mode there is no third, plain scan; the routine-looking grey-scale image is the mixed image, a weighted blend of the two tubes' reconstructions. Both readouts below come from the same acquisition:

begin
    """A blank drawing area at `position`: equal scales, no axes, limits `(x0, x1, y0, y1)`."""
    function canvas(position, limits; background = COLORS.paper)
        ax = Mke.Axis(position; aspect = Mke.DataAspect(), backgroundcolor = background)
        Mke.hidedecorations!(ax)
        Mke.hidespines!(ax)
        Mke.limits!(ax, limits...)
        return ax
    end

    """The corners of a rectangle centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, its corners rounded by `r`."""
    function rounded_rect(c, w, h, r)
        x0, y0, x1, y1 = c[1] - w / 2, c[2] - h / 2, c[1] + w / 2, c[2] + h / 2
        r = min(r, w / 2, h / 2)
        arc(cx, cy, θ0) = [
            Mke.Point2f(cx + r * cos(θ), cy + r * sin(θ))
            for θ in range(θ0, θ0 + π / 2; length = 8)
        ]
        return vcat(
            arc(x1 - r, y0 + r, -π / 2),
            arc(x1 - r, y1 - r, 0.0),
            arc(x0 + r, y1 - r, π / 2),
            arc(x0 + r, y0 + r, π),
        )
    end

    """A straight arrow from `a` to `b`; `head` is the arrowhead's size in pixels."""
    function arrow!(
        ax,
        a,
        b;
        color = COLORS.muted,
        linewidth = 2.5,
        head = 15,
        linestyle = :solid,
    )
        a, b = Mke.Point2f(a), Mke.Point2f(b)
        Mke.lines!(ax, [a, b]; color, linewidth, linestyle)
        t = b - a
        Mke.scatter!(
            ax,
            [b];
            marker = :utriangle,
            markersize = head,
            rotation = atan(t[2], t[1]) - π / 2,
            color,
            markerspace = :pixel,
        )
        return nothing
    end

    """
    A box in a flow chart: centred at `c`, `w` × `h`, a bold `title` and an optional smaller
    `subtitle`. `accent` colours its outline (and a strip down its left edge).
    """
    function node!(
        ax,
        c,
        title;
        subtitle = "",
        w = 3.0,
        h = 1.0,
        accent = COLORS.violet,
        fill = COLORS.card,
        textcolor = COLORS.ink,
        subcolor = COLORS.muted,
        titlesize = 19,
        subtitlesize = 15,
        code = false,
    )
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            rounded_rect(c, w, h, 0.14);
            color = fill,
            strokecolor = accent,
            strokewidth = 2,
        )
        strip = rounded_rect((c[1] - w / 2 + 0.06, c[2]), 0.12, h - 0.1, 0.05)
        Mke.poly!(ax, strip; color = accent)
        font = code ? "DejaVu Sans Mono Bold" : :bold
        dy = isempty(subtitle) ? 0.0 : 0.17 * h
        Mke.text!(
            ax,
            c[1] + 0.05,
            c[2] + dy;
            text = title,
            align = (:center, :center),
            fontsize = titlesize,
            font,
            color = textcolor,
        )
        isempty(subtitle) ||
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                c[1] + 0.05,
                c[2] - 0.22 * h;
                text = subtitle,
                align = (:center, :center),
                fontsize = subtitlesize,
                color = subcolor,
            )
        return nothing
    end

    """
    A flow chart: `nodes` maps a key to `(x, y, title, subtitle, accent)` (subtitle and accent
    optional), `edges` lists `from => to` pairs, drawn as arrows between the boxes' edges, and
    `labels` (optional) puts a note on an edge. Returns the canvas.
    """
    function flow_chart!(position, nodes, edges; limits, w = 3.0, h = 1.0, labels = Dict())
        ax = canvas(position, limits)
        box(key) = nodes[key]
        function port(from, to)
            a, b = box(from), box(to)
            if abs(b[2] - a[2]) < 1.0e-6
                # side by side
                s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
                return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
            elseif abs(b[1] - a[1]) < 1.0e-6
                # one above the other
                s = sign(b[2] - a[2])
                return (a[1], a[2] + s * h / 2), (b[1], b[2] - s * h / 2)
            else
                # leave sideways, arrive on the facing side
                s = sign(b[1] - a[1])
                return (a[1] + s * w / 2, a[2]), (b[1] - s * w / 2, b[2])
            end
        end
        for (from, to) in edges
            p, q = port(from, to)
            if abs(p[1] - q[1]) < 1.0e-6 || abs(p[2] - q[2]) < 1.0e-6
                # straight across or straight down
                arrow!(ax, p, q)
            else
                # a right-angled connector: across to the gap's middle, along it, then in
                mx = (p[1] + q[1]) / 2
                Mke.lines!(
                    ax,
                    Mke.Point2f[p, (mx, p[2]), (mx, q[2])];
                    color = COLORS.muted,
                    linewidth = 2.5,
                )
                arrow!(ax, (mx, q[2]), q)
            end
            haskey(labels, from => to) &&
                Mke.text!(
                    ax,
                    (p[1] + q[1]) / 2,
                    q[2] + 0.12;
                    text = labels[from => to],
                    align = (:center, :bottom),
                    fontsize = 15,
                    color = COLORS.muted,
                )
        end
        for (_, n) in nodes
            node!(
                ax,
                (n[1], n[2]),
                n[3];
                subtitle = length(n) >= 4 ? n[4] : "",
                accent = length(n) >= 5 ? n[5] : COLORS.violet,
                w,
                h,
            )
        end
        return ax
    end

    """
    A CT gantry seen along z, centred at the origin: the source(s) at radius `sid` (one per entry
    of `angles`, degrees), the fan, the detector arc at `sdd` from each source, and a round object
    of radius `r_object`. Draws on `ax` in the colours of `dark` (the locator band) or paper.
    """
    function gantry!(
        ax;
        sid = 5.4,
        sdd = 9.5,
        angles = (90.0,),
        fan_deg = 50.0,
        r_object = 2.0,
        detector_colors = (COLORS.cyan,),
        labels = ("Tube",),
        dark = true,
        object = true,
    )
        ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
        ring = dark ? COLORS.night_card : COLORS.card
        Mke.poly!(ax, Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid + 0.9); color = ring)
        Mke.poly!(
            ax,
            Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), sid - 1.6);
            color = dark ? COLORS.night : COLORS.paper,
        )
        for (k, θ) in enumerate(angles)
            θ = deg2rad(θ)
            s = Mke.Point2f(sid * cos(θ), sid * sin(θ))
            half = deg2rad(fan_deg / 2)
            # the fan, from the focal spot to the detector arc (a circle about the source)
            edge = Mke.Point2f[
                s + sdd * Mke.Point2f(cos(θ + π + φ), sin(θ + π + φ))
                for φ in range(-half, half; length = 40)
            ]
            Mke.poly!(
                ax,
                Mke.Point2f.(vcat([s], edge));
                color = (COLORS.beam, 0.22),
                strokewidth = 0,
            )
            Mke.lines!(ax, edge; color = detector_colors[mod1(k, end)], linewidth = 9)
            Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :rect, markersize = 26, color = ink)
            Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :circle, markersize = 9, color = COLORS.beam)
            Mke.text!(
                ax,
                s * 1.18;
                text = labels[mod1(k, end)],
                align = (:center, :center),
                fontsize = 17,
                font = :bold,
                color = ink,
            )
        end
        object &&
            Mke.poly!(
                ax,
                Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), r_object);
                color = (COLORS.blue, 0.55),
                strokecolor = ink,
                strokewidth = 1.5,
            )
        return ax
    end

    """
    The dark locator band that opens a notebook: `n` panels side by side, each a canvas with
    `limits`, its `titles[i]` and `subtitles[i]` underneath. Returns the figure and the canvases;
    draw into them, then show the figure.
    """
    function locator_band(titles, subtitles; limits, size = (1500, 560))
        fig = Mke.Figure(;
            size,
            backgroundcolor = COLORS.night,
            figure_padding = (10, 10, 18, 10),
        )
        axes = [
            canvas(fig[1, i], limits[i]; background = COLORS.night)
            for i in eachindex(titles)
        ]
        for i in eachindex(titles)
            Mke.Label(
                fig[2, i],
                titles[i];
                fontsize = 25,
                font = :bold,
                color = COLORS.night_ink,
                tellwidth = false,
            )
            Mke.Label(
                fig[3, i],
                subtitles[i];
                fontsize = 17,
                color = COLORS.night_muted,
                tellwidth = false,
            )
        end
        Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 1, 8)
        Mke.rowgap!(fig.layout, 2, 2)
        return fig, axes
    end
end;
const HU_WINDOW = (-200, 500); # every HU image's display window: soft tissue
slice_panel!

An image panel at position: slice on a square axis without ticks, in colormap over colorrange. Returns the axis.

"""
An image panel at `position`: `slice` on a square axis without ticks, in `colormap` over
`colorrange`. Returns the axis.
"""
function slice_panel!(
    position,
    slice;
    title = "",
    colormap = :grays,
    colorrange = HU_WINDOW,
)
    ax = Mke.Axis(position; title, aspect = Mke.DataAspect())
    Mke.hidedecorations!(ax)
    Mke.hidespines!(ax)
    Mke.heatmap!(ax, slice; colormap, colorrange)
    return ax
end
# The Gammex 472 as the drawings show it, measured from the phantom's own labels (cm from the
# centre): the body, and the centres of the calcium (labels 10–16) and iodine (20–26) rods
GAMMEX = let
    mask = phantom_cpu.mask[:, :, 1]
    a = phantom_cpu.voxel_size[1]
    n = size(mask, 1)
    function centre(label)
        idx = findall(==(UInt8(label)), mask)
        return (
            (sum(c -> c[1], idx) / length(idx) - (n + 1) / 2) * a,
            (sum(c -> c[2], idx) / length(idx) - (n + 1) / 2) * a,
        )
    end
    (
        body_r = sqrt(count(!=(0), mask) * a^2 / π),
        rod_r = sqrt(count(==(UInt8(10)), mask) * a^2 / π),
        calcium = [centre(l) for l in 10:16],
        iodine = [centre(l) for l in 20:26],
    )
end;
gammex!

Draw the Gammex 472 seen along z on ax (cm): the solid-water body, the seven calcium rods (inner ring) and the seven iodine rods (outer ring). calcium and iodine colour the rods (one colour, or one per rod); scale shrinks the drawing (into a gantry, say); dark draws it for the locator band.

"""
Draw the Gammex 472 seen along z on `ax` (cm): the solid-water body, the seven calcium rods
(inner ring) and the seven iodine rods (outer ring). `calcium` and `iodine` colour the rods (one
colour, or one per rod); `scale` shrinks the drawing (into a gantry, say); `dark` draws it for the
locator band.
"""
function gammex!(
    ax,
    g = GAMMEX;
    calcium = COLORS.red,
    iodine = COLORS.green,
    scale = 1.0,
    dark = false,
)
    ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
    Mke.poly!(
        ax,
        Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(0, 0), scale * g.body_r);
        color = (COLORS.blue, dark ? 0.55 : 0.18),
        strokecolor = (ink, 0.6),
        strokewidth = 1.5,
    )
    for (centres, colors) in ((g.calcium, calcium), (g.iodine, iodine))
        for (k, c) in enumerate(centres)
            color = colors isa AbstractVector ? colors[k] : colors
            Mke.poly!(
                ax,
                Mke.Circle(Mke.Point2f(scale .* c), scale * g.rod_r);
                color,
                strokecolor = (ink, 0.5),
                strokewidth = 1,
            )
        end
    end
    return ax
end
roi!

Shade the in-plane region mask (a Bool matrix on a fov_cm grid centred on the isocentre) on a drawing in cm.

"""
Shade the in-plane region `mask` (a Bool matrix on a `fov_cm` grid centred on the isocentre) on a
drawing in cm.
"""
function roi!(ax, mask, fov_cm; color = COLORS.violet, alpha = 0.75)
    n = size(mask, 1)
    xs = ((1:n) .- (n + 1) / 2) .* (fov_cm / n)
    Mke.heatmap!(
        ax,
        xs,
        xs,
        [m ? 1.0f0 : NaN32 for m in mask];
        colormap = [color, color],
        alpha,
        nan_color = :transparent,
    )
    return ax
end
tube_fan!

One tube of a CT gantry to scale (cm, the isocentre at the origin): the focal spot at sid and angle θ (degrees), the fan that covers a field of view of diameter fov, and its detector arc at sdd from the focal spot. (The kit's gantry! gives every tube one fan; the Force's two differ.)

"""
One tube of a CT gantry to scale (cm, the isocentre at the origin): the focal spot at `sid` and
angle `θ` (degrees), the fan that covers a field of view of diameter `fov`, and its detector arc at
`sdd` from the focal spot. (The kit's `gantry!` gives every tube one fan; the Force's two differ.)
"""
function tube_fan!(
    ax,
    θ;
    fov,
    sid = 59.5,
    sdd = 108.56,
    color = COLORS.cyan,
    label = "Tube",
    dark = false,
)
    ink = dark ? COLORS.night_ink : COLORS.ink
    θ = deg2rad(θ)
    s = Mke.Point2f(sid * cos(θ), sid * sin(θ))
    half = asin(fov / 2 / sid)
    edge = Mke.Point2f[
        s + sdd * Mke.Point2f(cos(θ + π + φ), sin(θ + π + φ))
        for φ in range(-half, half; length = 40)
    ]
    Mke.poly!(ax, vcat([s], edge); color = (COLORS.beam, 0.2), strokewidth = 0)
    Mke.lines!(ax, edge; color, linewidth = 9)
    Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :rect, markersize = 26, color = ink)
    Mke.scatter!(ax, [s]; marker = :circle, markersize = 9, color = COLORS.beam)
    Mke.text!(
        ax,
        s * 1.16;
        text = label,
        align = (:center, :center),
        fontsize = 17,
        font = :bold,
        color = ink,
    )
    return ax
end

1. The UFC Detector Table

The Force's detector is UFC, Siemens' Gd₂O₂S ceramic, 1.4 mm deep. Its response is BS.UFC_MC_EFFICIENCY_LUT, a Geant4 flat-field run (BasisMonteCarlo notebook 04_siemens_force.jl, 100 000 photons per keV from 1 to 140 keV): the efficiency is the energy a dexel collects per photon divided by the photon's energy. Three features are fluorescence and transmission, which Beer–Lambert absorption cannot model:

  1. The Gd K-edge, 50.24 keV: the efficiency falls from 0.935 to 0.791 between 50 and 51 keV. Above the edge a photon is absorbed more readily, but the 43 keV Gd K x ray it frees often escapes, carrying its energy away.

  2. Gd L-edge structure near 7–8 keV: the small dip at 8 keV.

  3. The high-energy roll-off, 0.857 at 100 keV to 0.612 at 140 keV, as photons pass through 1.4 mm or Compton-scatter out.

<details><summary>How the table enters the simulation</summary>

SOMATOM_FORCE has detector_material = :ufc and, by default, use_detector_efficiency = true. A photon of energy $E$ then leaves a mean signal $m_1 = E\,\mathrm{efficiency}(E)$ and a mean square $m_2 = m_1^2 / \mathrm{dqe0}(E)$ (dqe0, the zero-frequency DQE of one energy, adds the spread of the collected energy to the absorption). The detector reads $\sum_E w(E)\, m_1(E)\, e^{-\int \mu\, dl}$ with variance $\sum_E w(E)\, m_2(E)\, e^{-\int \mu\, dl}$. The spectral basis (spectral_basis(ws, protocol)) and the beam-hardening calibration (resolve_source_spectrum_full) weight the spectrum by the same $m_1$, so the forward and inverse spectral models match exactly. </details>

2. The Phantom: Gammex 472

A 33 cm solid-water cylinder with seven calcium rods (50–600 mg/mL) on an inner ring and seven iodine rods (2–20 mg/mL) on an outer ring, voxelized at 512² over 35 cm, 16 slices over 1 cm.

phantom_cpu = BS.create_gammex_472(
    n_voxels = 512,
    n_slices = 16,
    fov_cm = 35.0,
    z_cm = 1.0,
);
phantom = BS.Phantom(
    to_gpu(phantom_cpu.mask),
    phantom_cpu.materials,
    phantom_cpu.voxel_size,
    phantom_cpu.origin,
    phantom_cpu.extent,
);

3. The Scanner: SOMATOM Force

Third-generation dual source: two Vectron tubes and two Stellar Infinity UFC detectors, 95° apart in one gantry. Detector A covers a 50 cm field, detector B 35.5 cm. The geometry was measured on a clinical Force by Wang et al.

<details><summary>Every number and its source</summary>

ParameterValueSource
Source–isocenter (SID)595.0 mmWang et al. 2021, arXiv:2001.09471 §IV
Source–detector (SDD)1085.6 mmWang et al. 2021
Tube A–B angular offset95° (z-offset 0.88 mm)Siemens Force whitepaper; Wang et al.
Detector A channels920 (50 cm FOV)Wang et al.; whitepaper §1.2
Detector B channels640 (35.5 cm FOV)Wang et al.; Flohr/Schmidt DE-DSCT chapter
Rows96 × 0.6 mm at iso (57.6 mm z-coverage)whitepaper §1.2
Column pitch at iso0.054°/ch ≈ 0.561 mmWang et al. (1.023 mm at detector / 1.825× mag)
ScintillatorUFC Gd₂O₂S:Pr,Ce, ρ ≈ 7.34 g/cm³Siemens UFC page; Rossner & Grabmaier 1991
Tube (Vectron)2 × 120 kW, 70–150 kVp / 10 kV steps, ≤1300 mAwhitepaper §1.1; datasheet
Focal spots0.4×0.5 mm² smallest; ~0.8 / 1.2 mm nominalwhitepaper; Duan AAPM 2014
Tin filter0.6 mm Sn on the high-kV tube (SnX modes)Faby et al. Siemens DECT white paper; PMC12745887
Rotation0.25 s min (0.5 s routine)whitepaper
Projections1160 / rotation per focal-spot positionFlohr et al. Med Phys 2005 (Siemens family figure)

</details>

<details><summary>Modelling assumptions where no public source exists</summary>

  • Anode angle: Vectron's is unpublished, so the IPEM 8° spectrum (typical CT anodes are 7–9°).

  • Flat filtration: unpublished, so 3.0 mm Al + 0.9 mm Ti, the Vectron-family stack the NAEOTOM Alpha model uses (notebook 08). The 0.6 mm Sn is added on tube B only.

  • Bowtie: Siemens' body bowtie is unpublished, so CatSim's large-body profile stands in (as in notebooks 04 and 08).

  • Scintillator depth 1.4 mm, fill factor 0.9: proprietary. 1.4 mm is the only UFC thickness Siemens quotes and the depth of the Geant4 table. The fill factor scales the quanta a dexel collects, so it sets the noise, and cancels in the air calibration.

  • Electronic noise 0: the Stellar's TrueSignal ASIC has no published absolute noise figure; its design point is "electronic noise negligible against quantum noise" (Duan et al., AJR 2013).

</details>

<details><summary>Two tubes as two co-registered scans</summary>

As notebook 03 models rapid kVp switching as two scans, the Force's two tubes are two CTProtocols run on one EICTScanner, each with its own noise seed:

  • Detector arc: tube B gets detector A's 920-column arc, so the low- and high-energy sinograms are co-registered ray by ray for the decomposition. The 33 cm Gammex fits inside detector B's real 35.5 cm field, so no ray used here is missing on the real detector B.

  • The 95° offset: both scans cover a full rotation on the same angle grid, which is what the clinical rebinning produces when it aligns B onto A; a constant angular offset does nothing to a full-rotation axial scan.

  • Tube B's 0.88 mm z-offset: modelled by shifting the phantom origin −0.88 mm in z for tube B (section 6). For the z-invariant Gammex this is exactly nothing, but z-varying phantoms (XCAT, QRM) inherit the real misalignment.

  • Collimation: the Force reads 128 × 0.6 mm in dual-energy mode; this notebook uses 4.8 mm (8 × 0.6 mm), the thin-collimation equivalent that fits the 1 cm Gammex, as notebook 03 uses 5 mm.

</details>

# Tube and detector A's geometry, shared by both modelled tubes (see above)
scanner = BS.SOMATOM_FORCE;

4. The Protocols: One Dual-Energy Acquisition

The Force's clinical abdomen pairs are x / Sn150 (x from 70 to 100 kVp, 0.6 mm Sn on tube B). The bundled IPEM spectra stop at 140 kVp, so this notebook runs 100 / Sn140, the pair the Definition Flash ran clinically (with 0.4 mm Sn; the Force's 0.6 mm is kept). The mean energies are within about 2 keV of the 100 / Sn150 target. The currents follow the published Force abdomen 100 / Sn150 reference, 190 and 95 mAs at 0.5 s, a 2 : 1 split.

TubekVpFiltersmAViewsRotation
A (low)1003 mm Al + 0.9 mm Ti38011600.5 s
B (high)1403 mm Al + 0.9 mm Ti + 0.6 mm Sn19011600.5 s
protocol_low = BS.CTProtocol(
    kVp = 100,
    mA = 380.0,
    views = 1160,
    rotation_time = 0.5,
    collimation_mm = 4.8, # nominal beam width; axial cone guards are automatic
    additional_filters = [("Ti", 0.9)],
);
protocol_high = BS.CTProtocol(
    kVp = 140,
    mA = 190.0,
    views = 1160,
    rotation_time = 0.5,
    collimation_mm = 4.8,
    additional_filters = [("Ti", 0.9), ("Sn", 0.6)],
);
"""
    ufc_detected_spectrum(protocol) -> (e, w_eta)

Display helper: tube spectrum × flat filtration × protocol filters (IPEM, absolute flux) × the
UFC's signal per photon, `E·efficiency(E)`: what the detector integrates (centre ray, no bowtie).
"""
function ufc_detected_spectrum(protocol)
    e, w = BS.resolve_source_spectrum_without_bowtie(
        force_opts,
        protocol;
        scanner = scanner,
    )
    t = BS.UFC_MC_EFFICIENCY_LUT # 1 keV grid: index = energy
    eff(E) = (
        i = clamp(floor(Int, E), 1, 139);
        f = E - i;
        (1 - f) * t.efficiency[i] + f * t.efficiency[i + 1]
    )
    return e, Float64.(w) .* e .* eff.(e)
end;

5. Physics Switches and Noise Draws

force_opts are the physics switches the basis-spectral-denoising study settled on for its dual-source scanner, applied to the Force:

  • Detector response: the scanner reads the UFC Geant4 table; every energy is weighted by its signal per photon $m_1$, and the noise is compound Poisson with $m_2 = m_1^2/\mathrm{dqe0}$, so its variance per unit signal rises as the beam hardens.

  • Heel effect off, which keeps the forward spectral model equal to the response the spectral basis inverts (at 4.8 mm collimation the heel is a small row-direction effect).

  • View integration, view_samples = 5: a detector integrates while the gantry turns, so each view reads the object averaged over the arc it sweeps, a blur largest far from the isocentre that the noise, counted once per view, does not share. Each Force tube reads its own detector for the whole view period (view_arc = 1.0).

Each tube has its own seed: the two tube-detector chains are physically independent, and two acquisitions drawn from one seed would carry correlated noise that the decomposition amplifies. Draw 0 is the noise-free expectation; draw $r ≥ 1$ gives each tube the seed $\mathrm{seed} + 1000\,(r - 1)$.

begin
    VIEW_SAMPLES = 5
    force_opts = BS.SimOptions(
        projector = :dd_fast,
        use_heel_effect = false,
        view_samples = VIEW_SAMPLES,
    )
    "The same physics switches with one field replaced."
    with_option(opts, field, value) = BS.SimOptions(;
        (f => getfield(opts, f) for f in fieldnames(BS.SimOptions) if f !== field)...,
        (field => value,)...,
    )
end;
begin
    # The two exposures: tube A sees the phantom, tube B the phantom through its −0.88 mm z-offset.
    # Draw 0 is the noise-free expectation; draw r ≥ 1 gives each tube the seed `seed + 1000 (r − 1)`,
    # so the tubes stay independent within a draw, and draws of each other.
    EXPOSURES = [
        (
            label = "100 kVp",
            protocol = protocol_low,
            seed = 1234,
            view_arc = 1.0,
            tube = :a,
        ),
        (
            label = "Sn140 kVp",
            protocol = protocol_high,
            seed = 4321,
            view_arc = 1.0,
            tube = :b,
        ),
    ]
    DE_DRAWS = (reference = 0, measured = 1, calibration = 9)
    realization_seed(e, r) = e.seed + 1000 * (max(r, 1) - 1)
    opts_for(e, r) = with_option(
        with_option(
            with_option(force_opts, :seed, realization_seed(e, r)),
            :use_noise,
            r > 0,
        ),
        :view_arc,
        e.view_arc,
    )
end;
# The centred 5 × 0.6 mm grid. The axial workspace adds symmetric detector guard rows, so the
# peripheral voxels of both end slices keep measured cone-beam support.
recon_opts = BS.ReconOptions(matrix_size = (512, 512, 5), fov_cm = 35.0, z_cm = 0.3);

6. The Acquisition: One Projection per Tube, Three Draws

acquire builds each tube's workspace and projects it once: everything before the noise is the same for every draw, so the first draw keeps the projection (keep_projection = true) and the others pass it back (projection) and draw only their noise, exactly as if simulated afresh.

DrawNoiseUsed for
0offthe noise-free reference every noisy result is scored against
1onthe measured acquisition every result comes from
9onthe calibration draw, which only fixes the reconstruction's pair (section 8)

The first draw also keeps each tube's one-channel spectral basis, spectral_basis(ws, protocol): every ray's detected spectrum (source × filtration × bowtie × the UFC's $m_1$), the model the projector applied, scaled to the ray's noise-equivalent quanta in air. Tube B sees the phantom through the real −0.88 mm z-offset of detector B (Wang et al. 2021).

# Tube B's view of the phantom: the origin shifted by the real −0.88 mm detector z-offset (nothing
# changes for the z-invariant Gammex)
phantom_b = BS.Phantom(
    phantom.mask,
    phantom.materials,
    phantom.voxel_size,
    (phantom.origin[1], phantom.origin[2], phantom.origin[3] - 0.088),
    phantom.extent,
);
"""
    acquire(draws) -> Dict{Int, NamedTuple}

The DE acquisition of the Gammex (`EXPOSURES`, both tubes) for every draw in `draws`: draw 0 the
noise-free expectation, draw `r ≥ 1` a noisy realisation with the seeds `realization_seed(e, r)`.
Each tube is projected once, by the first draw, and every other draw re-uses that projection
(`keep_projection`, `projection`), only its noise drawn. Each entry holds the two log-transmission
channels, the spectral basis (shared by every draw), the geometry and the wall time per tube.
"""
function acquire(draws)
    parts = map(EXPOSURES) do e
        ph = e.tube === :b ? phantom_b : phantom
        projection = nothing
        channels = Dict{Int, Array{Float32, 3}}()
        seconds = Dict{Int, Float64}()
        model = nothing
        for r in draws
            opts = opts_for(e, r)
            t = time()
            ws = BS.create_workspace(scanner, e.protocol, opts, recon_opts, ph)
            try
                result = BS.simulate!(
                    ws,
                    ph,
                    e.protocol,
                    opts;
                    report_dose = false,
                    keep_projection = projection === nothing,
                    projection,
                )
                projection === nothing && (projection = result.projection)
                channels[r] = Array(ws.sinogram)
                if model === nothing
                    model = (geom = ws.geom, basis = BS.spectral_basis(ws, e.protocol))
                end
            finally
                BS.release_backend!(ws)
            end
            seconds[r] = time() - t
        end
        projection = nothing
        (; channels, seconds, model...)
    end
    GC.gc(true)
    basis = BS.spectral_basis_from_acquisitions(acquisitions = [p.basis for p in parts])
    Dict(
        r => (
            draw = r,
            channels = [p.channels[r] for p in parts],
            basis = basis,
            geom = first(parts).geom,
            seconds = [p.seconds[r] for p in parts],
        )
        for r in draws
    )
end;
de_acq = acquire((DE_DRAWS.reference, DE_DRAWS.measured, DE_DRAWS.calibration));
DrawRoleSeeds (A, B)Seconds (A, B)
0noise-free referencenone67.2, 1.0
1measured1234, 43210.5, 0.4

Draw 0 projects each tube, 5 sub-views per view; draws 1 and 9 re-use that projection and only draw their noise (wall time on this render, compilation included in the first call).

# The measured draw: every result below comes from it.
de_measured = de_acq[DE_DRAWS.measured];

7. The Mixed Image

In dual-energy mode the routine-looking output is the mixed image, a linear blend of the two tubes' reconstructions, $M = w\,I_\mathrm{low} + (1 - w)\,I_\mathrm{high}$ (Yu et al., Med Phys 2009; Eusemann et al., SPIE 2008); on Sn150-class pairs the clinical weight is 0.5–0.6 (Lenga et al., Br J Radiol 2021). Each tube runs notebook 01's correction stack on its own, a water beam-hardening correction (BHC) of the sinogram, FDK, then HU, before the blend. If the UFC table is folded in right, solid water lands at 0 HU in both tubes' images, and so in any blend.

The BHC sees the detected spectrum

The water polynomial must see the spectrum the forward model used: the bowtie-hardened spectrum of every column weighted by the UFC's signal per photon, $m_1(E) = E\,\eta(E)$ (resolve_source_spectrum_full), fed to the low-level calibrate_bhc_water(e, w_col), the per-column fit the high-level API performs, with the UFC included.

"""
    ufc_bhc_calibration(protocol, geom)

η-aware per-tube BHC: bowtie-hardened per-column spectrum × UFC η(E) →
per-column two-material polynomial.  Returns `(model, μ_water, ref_E_keV)`.
"""
function ufc_bhc_calibration(protocol, geom)
    # resolve_source_spectrum_full folds bowtie AND the src UFC η(E)
    # (via the same build_physics_config the forward model used).
    e, ŵ = BS.resolve_source_spectrum_full(
        force_opts,
        protocol;
        scanner = scanner,
        geom = geom,
    )
    e2, w_col = BS.bhc_spectrum_per_column(e, ŵ) # [n_E, n_col]

    # Single mono-equivalent target = mean energy of the η-folded mean spectrum
    w_mean = vec(sum(w_col; dims = 2)) ./ size(w_col, 2)
    ref_E = sum(e2 .* w_mean) / sum(w_mean)

    # Parameter-free water BHC from the custom UFC-η per-column spectrum — zero
    # segmentation thresholds (the two-material bone pass is deprecated:
    # its 450–600 HU window misclassified dense iodine as bone).
    model = BS.calibrate_bhc_water(e2, w_col; reference_energy_keV = ref_E)
    return (
        model = model,
        μ_water = model.μ_water_ref,
        ref_E_keV = model.reference_energy_keV,
    )
end;
"""
    ufc_poly_recon(sino_cpu, geom, bhc) -> Array{Float32, 3}

Doctrine correction stack for one tube: knobless water sino-BHC → FDK → HU.
"""
function ufc_poly_recon(sino_cpu, geom, bhc)
    matrix_size = recon_opts.matrix_size

    sino_gpu = to_gpu(sino_cpu)
    # Knobless water BHC: one sinogram-domain pass, no recon round-trip.
    sino_bhc = BS.apply_bhc_water(sino_gpu, bhc.model)
    sino_gpu = sino_bhc

    ws_fdk = BS.create_fdk_recon_workspace(sino_gpu, geom, matrix_size)
    recon_μ = BS.reconstruct!(ws_fdk, sino_gpu, geom)

    # (image-domain BHC + applied cupping removed — deprecated; cupping is a
    #  QA metric via measure_radial_cupping)
    hu = Float32.(BS.to_hounsfield(Array(recon_μ); μ_water = bhc.μ_water))

    ws_fdk = nothing
    sino_gpu = nothing
    recon_μ = nothing
    GC.gc(true)
    return hu
end;
bhc_low = ufc_bhc_calibration(protocol_low, de_measured.geom);
bhc_high = ufc_bhc_calibration(protocol_high, de_measured.geom);

The calibrations, with the UFC folded in: tube A's reference energy is 68.2 keV, where water attenuates 0.19487 cm⁻¹; tube B's is 100.8 keV, 0.17033 cm⁻¹.

hu_tube = (
    low = ufc_poly_recon(de_measured.channels[1], de_measured.geom, bhc_low),
    high = ufc_poly_recon(de_measured.channels[2], de_measured.geom, bhc_high),
);
# Siemens' linear mixed image, M = w·I_low + (1 − w)·I_high (image domain, Yu 2009); w = 0.5 is the
# common Sn150-pair default (0.3–0.7 clinically)
MIX_W_LOW = 0.5f0;
hu_mixed = MIX_W_LOW .* hu_tube.low .+ (1.0f0 - MIX_W_LOW) .* hu_tube.high;
# Solid water, eroded 12 pixels from every edge, in the three images (every slice)
poly_water_stats = let
    ERODE_PX = 12.0
    mask_2d_raw = phantom_cpu.mask[:, :, size(phantom_cpu.mask, 3) ÷ 2]
    sw_bool = BS.erode_mask_2d(
        mask_2d_raw .== UInt8(BS.REGION_SOLID_WATER);
        erode_px = ERODE_PX,
    )
    sw_idx = findall(sw_bool)
    n_z = size(hu_mixed, 3)

    function _stats(vol)
        vals = Float64[Float64(vol[ci, z]) for z in 1:n_z, ci in sw_idx]
        (mean = mean(vals), std = std(vals), n = length(vals))
    end
    (
        low = _stats(hu_tube.low),
        high = _stats(hu_tube.high),
        mixed = _stats(hu_mixed),
        mask_2d = collect(sw_bool),
    )
end;

8. The VMI Chain

The spectral basis. acquire merged the two tubes' bases with spectral_basis_from_acquisitions: their energy grids onto one union grid, each tube's per-ray detected spectrum scaled by its own noise-equivalent quanta in air ($I_0\,\mathrm{ff}\,S_1^2/S_2$). The likelihood thus sees the absolute response $\Phi_k(E)$ of every ray and channel (source × flat filters × bowtie × the UFC's $m_1(E)$), the model the projector applied. No calibration scan is involved, and all three draws share it.

basis = de_measured.basis;

The basis holds 2 channels on a 274-point energy grid for 920 × 8 rays; the response sums to the air counts to within 3.1e-8 (relative).

The chain. One package call goes from the two corrected sinograms to the VMIs, vmi_pipeline(; denoiser = SpectralHYPR(), fbp_filter, pair_basis, composite_energy):

  1. Projection HYPR-LR (ProjectionHYPR): a 3 × 3 window (columns × views of one parity, view_stride = 2, so the odd and even views stay independent) on each detector row's counts, each tube's dispersion measured on its own air rays.

  2. The K = 2 decomposition: per ray, the Poisson maximum-likelihood iodine and water pair under the exact polychromatic mean of both tubes, every detector row kept.

  3. The spectral pair (spectral_pair): FDK of the basis pair and of its odd- and even-view halves, whose difference measures the noise of everything downstream; the composite $M$ (the minimum-noise VMI) and its complement $I_\perp$, whose noise is uncorrelated with $M$'s.

  4. ACNR on the complement only; the composite stays as reconstructed.

  5. Image HYPR (ImageHYPR): the complement pooled within its slice, weighted by the composite, over the window with the least estimated risk.

  6. VMI synthesis at 50, 70, 100 and 140 keV from the one basis pair.

The pair and the composite energy come from the calibration draw. Near its minimum the VMI noise hardly changes with energy, so an argmin measured on the draw being evaluated would itself be noise. $E^*$ and $\beta$ come from the calibration draw's plain decomposition, the composite energy from its decomposition after the projection HYPR; the measured draw, the same draw without denoising, and the noise-free reference are then reconstructed alike.

One window, not a fitted pair: the Force has none

The other dual-energy notebooks reconstruct the composite and its complement with a PairFilter of two windows fitted, in basis-spectral-denoising, to the MTF and NPS of a physical Gammex scan on that scanner. No physical Force scan was fitted, so no Force pair exists, and the GE and Flash pairs do not transfer: a fitted pair absorbs everything that shapes one scanner's resolution and noise texture (its dexel pitch, 0.561 mm on the Force against 0.705 mm on the Flash, its focal spot, the vendor kernel of the series it was matched to). Both are reconstructed here with the soft-tissue SoftFilter().

# basis-spectral-denoising's HYPR_CHAIN: ProjectionHYPR(3 × 3 Box, view_stride = 2) and ImageHYPR()
HYPR_CHAIN = BS.SpectralHYPR();
VMI_CHAIN = (
    method = :nchannel,
    controls = BS.NChannelControls(),
    use_tlbf = false,
    antialias = true,
);
# One window for the composite and its complement alike: no fitted Force pair exists (see above).
FORCE_FILTER = BS.SoftFilter();
de_vmi_energies = [50.0, 70.0, 100.0, 140.0];
# `pair_basis` and `composite_energy` (basis-spectral-denoising's `PAIR_BASIS`), from the calibration draw
calibration = let a = de_acq[DE_DRAWS.calibration]
    decompose(denoiser) = BS.vmi_pipeline(;
        channels = a.channels,
        basis = a.basis,
        geom = a.geom,
        to_backend = to_gpu,
        matrix_size = recon_opts.matrix_size,
        vmi_energies = Tuple(de_vmi_energies),
        denoiser,
        keep_sinograms = true,
        VMI_CHAIN...,
        use_acnr = false,
    ).sinograms
    sp(d; kw...) = BS.spectral_pair(
        d.water,
        d.iodine,
        a.geom,
        recon_opts.matrix_size;
        filter = BS.SoftFilter(),
        antialias = VMI_CHAIN.antialias,
        to_backend = to_gpu,
        kw...,
    )
    x = sp(decompose(nothing)) # the plain decomposition
    c = sp(decompose(BS.SpectralHYPR(image = nothing)); # after the projection HYPR
        basis = (Estar = x.Estar, β = x.β)
    )
    (pair_basis = (Estar = x.Estar, β = x.β), composite_energy = c.Estar)
end;
de_vmi = BS.vmi_pipeline(;
    channels = de_measured.channels,
    basis,
    geom = de_measured.geom,
    to_backend = to_gpu,
    matrix_size = recon_opts.matrix_size,
    vmi_energies = Tuple(de_vmi_energies),
    denoiser = HYPR_CHAIN,
    fbp_filter = FORCE_FILTER,
    pair_basis = calibration.pair_basis,
    composite_energy = calibration.composite_energy,
    keep_sinograms = true,
    VMI_CHAIN...,
);
# The same draw and reconstruction without the denoising (no HYPR, no ACNR), and the noise-free
# reference (draw 0, the same projection), reconstructed alike.
de_none, de_ref = (
    BS.vmi_pipeline(;
        channels = de_acq[r].channels,
        basis,
        geom = de_measured.geom,
        to_backend = to_gpu,
        matrix_size = recon_opts.matrix_size,
        vmi_energies = Tuple(de_vmi_energies),
        denoiser = nothing,
        use_acnr = false,
        fbp_filter = FORCE_FILTER,
        pair_basis = calibration.pair_basis,
        composite_energy = calibration.composite_energy,
        VMI_CHAIN...,
    )
    for r in (DE_DRAWS.measured, DE_DRAWS.reference)
);

The decomposition solved 8537600 rays in 1.7 s with 2.4 outer iterations on average; 0.0% did not converge and 0.003% / 0.0% touched the iodine / water bounds. The projection HYPR measured dispersions (variance / mean of the counts on the air rays) of 1.0 and 1.0 for tube A and tube B.

From the calibration draw: the pair at E* = 79.0 keV, β = -0.00808, and the composite ACNR and the image HYPR act on at 77.0 keV. The image HYPR pooled the complement over a 31 × 31 window.

9. The VMIs

vmi_pipeline synthesizes each VMI from the basis pair (McCollough 2015): $\mu(E) = c_\mathrm{water}\,(\mu/\rho)_\mathrm{water}(E) + c_\mathrm{iodine}\,(\mu/\rho)_\mathrm{iodine}(E)$, in HU against water at the same energy. The rows are the measured draw without denoising, the measured draw through the whole chain, and the noise-free reference.

# The basis pair in the eroded solid water: a perfect decomposition reads water ≈ 1 g/mL (solid
# water is not pure water, so a small offset is expected) and iodine ≈ 0
solid_water_basis = let
    ERODE_PX = 12.0

    mask_2d_raw = phantom_cpu.mask[:, :, size(phantom_cpu.mask, 3) ÷ 2]
    sw_bool_raw = (mask_2d_raw .== UInt8(BS.REGION_SOLID_WATER))
    sw_bool = BS.erode_mask_2d(sw_bool_raw; erode_px = ERODE_PX)

    n_raw = count(sw_bool_raw)
    n_eroded = count(sw_bool)
    n_eroded == 0 &&
        error(
            "solid_water_basis: deep erosion (σ = $(ERODE_PX) px) wiped out the SW " *
                "ROI (raw count = $(n_raw)).  Reduce erode_px or check phantom mask.",
        )

    sw_idx = findall(sw_bool)
    _mean(vol) = mean(vol[ci, z] for z in axes(vol, 3) for ci in sw_idx)

    (
        c_water = Float64(_mean(de_vmi.images.water)),
        c_iodine = Float64(_mean(de_vmi.images.iodine)),
        n_voxels = length(sw_idx) * size(de_vmi.images.water, 3),
        mask_2d = collect(sw_bool),
    )
end;

In the eroded solid water the basis pair reads 0.9984 g/mL of water and 0.011 mg/mL of iodine (128360 voxels).

# The VMI stack as one volume per energy (keV → (nx, ny, nz) HU).
vmi_HU_final = Dict(
    Float64(E) => de_vmi.vmis[:, :, :, k]
    for (k, E) in pairs(de_vmi.energies)
);

10. Water: Accuracy and Noise

Water is the reference of the HU scale, so the eroded solid water should read close to 0 HU in every VMI (solid water is not pure water). The noise is measured in a central ROI against the noise-free reference, as the standard deviation of (VMI − reference): the reference shares the projection and the reconstruction, so the difference is noise alone, with no structure mixed in. The same draw without denoising shows what the chain removes.

const WATER_NOISE_ROI_RADIUS_PX = 12; # ≈ 8.2 mm at 0.683 mm per pixel
# A disc of WATER_NOISE_ROI_RADIUS_PX pixels at the centre of the reconstruction grid
water_noise_roi = let
    nx_r, ny_r, nz_r = size(de_vmi.images.water)
    cx = nx_r ÷ 2 + 1
    cy = ny_r ÷ 2 + 1
    r² = Float64(WATER_NOISE_ROI_RADIUS_PX)^2
    roi_bool = [(i - cx)^2 + (j - cy)^2 ≤ r² for i in 1:nx_r, j in 1:ny_r]
    n_vox = count(roi_bool)
    (
        center_xy = (Float64(cx), Float64(cy)),
        mask_2d = roi_bool,
        n_voxels = n_vox,
        n_total = n_vox * nz_r,
    )
end;
# Mean HU and noise in the central ROI at every energy: σ of (VMI − noise-free reference), with and
# without the denoising
vmi_noise_by_keV = let
    roi_idx = findall(water_noise_roi.mask_2d)
    nz_r = size(de_vmi.vmis, 3)
    vals(run, k) = Float64[Float64(run.vmis[ci, z, k]) for z in 1:nz_r, ci in roi_idx]

    out = Dict{Float64, NamedTuple}()
    for (k, E) in enumerate(de_vmi_energies)
        p, n, r = vals(de_vmi, k), vals(de_none, k), vals(de_ref, k)
        out[E] = (
            mean = mean(p),
            reference = mean(r),
            std = std(p .- r),
            std_none = std(n .- r),
            n = length(p),
        )
    end
    out
end;

11. The Rods Against Theory

Every rod's mean HU in an 8-pixel-radius ROI at its centroid, over every slice, against the theoretical HU of its material, $1000\,(\mu_\mathrm{rod}(E) - \mu_\mathrm{water}(E)) / \mu_\mathrm{water}(E)$ from BS.compute_μ_at_energy: pure physics, no fitting.

ROD_LABELS = (
    Ca = (UInt8(10), UInt8(11), UInt8(12), UInt8(13), UInt8(14), UInt8(15), UInt8(16)),
    I = (UInt8(20), UInt8(21), UInt8(22), UInt8(23), UInt8(24), UInt8(25), UInt8(26)),
);
ROD_NAMES = (
    Ca = (
        "50 mg/mL",
        "100 mg/mL",
        "200 mg/mL",
        "300 mg/mL",
        "400 mg/mL",
        "500 mg/mL",
        "600 mg/mL",
    ),
    I = (
        "2.0 mg/mL",
        "2.5 mg/mL",
        "5.0 mg/mL",
        "7.5 mg/mL",
        "10.0 mg/mL",
        "15.0 mg/mL",
        "20.0 mg/mL",
    ),
);
rod_data = let
    materials = phantom_cpu.materials
    mask_2d = phantom_cpu.mask[:, :, size(phantom_cpu.mask, 3) ÷ 2]
    nx, ny = size(mask_2d)
    ROI_RADIUS_PX = 8

    function rod_centroid(label::UInt8)
        idx = findall(==(label), mask_2d)
        isempty(idx) && error("rod_centroid: no voxels with label $label")
        cx = sum(ci -> Float64(ci[1]), idx) / length(idx)
        cy = sum(ci -> Float64(ci[2]), idx) / length(idx)
        return (cx, cy)
    end

    function rod_roi_mask(label::UInt8)
        cx, cy = rod_centroid(label)
        i_lo = max(1, floor(Int, cx - ROI_RADIUS_PX))
        i_hi = min(nx, ceil(Int, cx + ROI_RADIUS_PX))
        j_lo = max(1, floor(Int, cy - ROI_RADIUS_PX))
        j_hi = min(ny, ceil(Int, cy + ROI_RADIUS_PX))
        roi = CartesianIndex{2}[]
        r² = Float64(ROI_RADIUS_PX)^2
        for j in j_lo:j_hi, i in i_lo:i_hi
            ((i - cx)^2 + (j - cy)^2) ≤ r² && push!(roi, CartesianIndex(i, j))
        end
        return roi
    end

    rod_rois = Dict(
        lab => rod_roi_mask(lab)
        for lab in vcat(collect(ROD_LABELS.Ca), collect(ROD_LABELS.I))
    )

    μ_water_E = Dict(
        E => BS.compute_μ_at_energy(BS.XA.Materials.water, E)
        for E in de_vmi_energies
    )

    function theoretical_hu(material, E::Float64)
        μ = BS.compute_μ_at_energy(material, E)
        return 1000.0 * (μ - μ_water_E[E]) / μ_water_E[E]
    end

    function measured_hu(vmi_vol, label::UInt8)
        roi = rod_rois[label]
        return mean(vmi_vol[ci, z] for z in axes(vmi_vol, 3) for ci in roi)
    end

    out = Dict{Symbol, NamedTuple}()
    for group in (:Ca, :I)
        labels = ROD_LABELS[group]
        meas = [measured_hu(vmi_HU_final[E], lab) for lab in labels, E in de_vmi_energies]
        theo = [
            theoretical_hu(materials[Int(lab) + 1], E) # material entry L + 1 is label L
            for lab in labels, E in de_vmi_energies
        ]
        out[group] = (
            labels = labels,
            names = ROD_NAMES[group],
            measured = meas,
            theoretical = theo,
        )
    end
    out
end;
# The least-squares line of measured against theoretical HU, per rod group and energy
rod_fits = let
    function fit_lr(x, y)
        x̄, ȳ = mean(x), mean(y)
        β = sum((x .- x̄) .* (y .- ȳ)) / sum((x .- x̄).^2)
        α = ȳ - β * x̄
        ŷ = α .+ β .* x
        ss_res = sum((y .- ŷ).^2)
        (
            slope = β,
            intercept = α,
            r² = 1 - ss_res / sum((y .- ȳ).^2),
            rmse = sqrt(ss_res / length(y)),
        )
    end
    Dict(
        (group, E) => fit_lr(
            rod_data[group].theoretical[:, j],
            rod_data[group].measured[:, j],
        )
        for group in (:Ca, :I)
        for (j, E) in enumerate(de_vmi_energies)
    )
end;
